Overexpression in SW13vim- cells reflects relevant assembly properties of GFAP.
evaluation.notes: The authors appropriately note in the discussion that overexpression in cancer cell lines may not reflect astrocyte signaling.

nodes.label: Electron micrographs of in vitro assembled purified GFAP show that S13A forms ab…
nodes.claim: Electron micrographs of in vitro assembled purified GFAP show that S13A forms abnormally short filaments, while S13D forms only globular structures.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Electron micrographs showing the filament properties of in vitro assembled GFAP (WT, S13A and S13D).

strengths: In vitro assembly with purified protein eliminates confounding cellular factors.
EM provides direct, high-resolution visualization of filament vs. globular structures.
The results are consistent with the cell-based findings, providing cross-validation.
The observation that S13D forms homogeneous globular structures (not aggregates) in vitro is an important mechanistic distinction from the cell-based aggregation phenotype.
weaknesses: Representative images are shown but quantitative analysis of filament length for S13A or particle size for S13D is not provided.
It is unclear how many independent preparations/assembly reactions were performed.
The claim is purely descriptive; no quantitative metrics are provided.
alternative_interpretations: The inability of S13D to form filaments in vitro could reflect the specific structural perturbation of the D substitution rather than mimicry of phosphorylation per se.
required_assumptions: In vitro assembly conditions are relevant to in vivo filament formation.
The aspartate substitution at position 13 structurally mimics phosphoserine.
evaluation.notes: The disconnect between globular structures in vitro and aggregates in cells is interesting and noted by the authors, suggesting cell-specific factors contribute to aggregation.

nodes.label: pSer13-GFAP signal was unexpectedly also present in isogenic control astrocytes,…
nodes.claim: pSer13-GFAP signal was unexpectedly also present in isogenic control astrocytes, possibly triggered by in vitro culture conditions, but its organization was filamentous rather than aggregated.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Somewhat surprisingly, we also observed pSer13-GFAP signal in the isogenic control cells, possibly triggered by the in vitro culture conditions.

strengths: The authors transparently report this unexpected finding rather than omitting it.
They note the key qualitative difference: filamentous vs. aggregated organization of pSer13-GFAP in control vs. AxD astrocytes.
The observation is internally consistent — what matters for disease is not just phosphorylation but its context (AxD mutation).
weaknesses: The presence of pSer13 signal in isogenic controls complicates the interpretation that pSer13 is disease-specific, as claimed for human brain tissue.
The explanation ('possibly triggered by in vitro culture conditions') is speculative and not tested.
This finding raises questions about the disease specificity of pSer13-GFAP as observed in human tissues — could it also be present in control brains at levels below detection?
Potential tension with c1.1.3.1 which states generally no pSer13 signal in control brains.
alternative_interpretations: pSer13-GFAP may be a normal regulatory modification that becomes pathological only when combined with AxD mutations, rather than a disease-specific mark.
In vitro culture stress could activate kinases that normally don't phosphorylate GFAP in vivo, making the cell model less physiologically relevant for this particular readout.
required_assumptions: The pSer13 signal in isogenic controls is culture-induced and not reflective of normal in vivo astrocyte biology.
The qualitative difference in pSer13-GFAP organization (filamentous vs. aggregated) is the disease-relevant distinction.
evaluation.notes: This finding potentially weakens the narrative that pSer13 is an AxD-specific marker, though the distinction between filamentous and aggregated pSer13 organization is meaningful. Relates to c1.1.3.1.

nodes.label: Electron microscopy of AxD iPSC-astrocytes revealed large juxtanuclear fibrous b…
nodes.claim: Electron microscopy of AxD iPSC-astrocytes revealed large juxtanuclear fibrous bundles at nuclear invaginations, with an intact nuclear envelope.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Electron microscopy images of AxD patient iPSC-astrocytes revealing large, juxtanuclear fibrous bundles

strengths: EM is the gold standard for ultrastructural analysis.
The observation of intact nuclear envelope is important for understanding the nature of nuclear invaginations.
The finding is consistent with previous EM studies of AxD mouse models and patient tissue (Sosunov et al., 2017).
weaknesses: Only representative images are shown; quantification of the frequency of invaginations or fibrous bundles is not provided.
It is unclear how many cells were examined by EM.
Only AxD cells appear to have been examined by EM; comparison with isogenic control cells would strengthen the claim.
The authors themselves note these are not identical to electron-dense RFs in post-mortem brain.
alternative_interpretations: Juxtanuclear fibrous bundles could be a common feature of IF-expressing cells in culture and not specific to AxD.
Nuclear invaginations can occur in many cell types under various conditions and may not be disease-specific.
required_assumptions: The EM images are representative of the overall cell population.
Nuclear invaginations in iPSC-astrocytes reflect the pathology seen in AxD patient brains.
evaluation.notes: The authors appropriately qualify their interpretation, noting that these structures may represent an intermediate state.

nodes.label: Immunoblot analysis shows significantly higher cleaved GFAP in S13D and S13E com…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot analysis shows significantly higher cleaved GFAP in S13D and S13E compared to WT (p<0.05, two-way ANOVA, n=3 independent experiments).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of panel A by densitometry shows cleaved and full-length GFAP in phospho-mutants relative to WT GFAP (mean ± SD from three independent experiments; *p<0.05 two-way ANOVA).

strengths: Statistical analysis is reported (p<0.05, two-way ANOVA).
Three independent experiments provide biological replication.
The 24 kDa fragment is consistent with the known caspase-6 cleavage product described by Chen et al. (2013).
weaknesses: p<0.05 with n=3 is modest statistical evidence.
The two-way ANOVA is appropriate but the specific comparisons and correction for multiple comparisons are not detailed.
The connection between phospho-mimicry and caspase cleavage is correlative in this overexpression system.
SW13vim- cells may not reflect the caspase activity present in astrocytes.
alternative_interpretations: The increased cleavage could be due to altered protein folding/stability of the S13D/E mutants rather than a direct effect of phosphorylation on caspase accessibility.
Overexpression-induced stress could activate caspases, and the phospho-mimic mutants may simply aggregate more, triggering more stress.
required_assumptions: Phospho-mimic mutations replicate the effects of phosphorylation on caspase accessibility.
The GA5 antibody specifically detects the 24 kDa C-terminal caspase-6 cleavage product.
evaluation.notes: The mechanistic link between phosphorylation and caspase cleavage remains correlative, as the authors acknowledge.

nodes.label: Caspase-6 inhibitor treatment reduced cleavage of S13D and S13D/R79H GFAP (p<0.0…
nodes.claim: Caspase-6 inhibitor treatment reduced cleavage of S13D and S13D/R79H GFAP (p<0.01 and p<0.0001 respectively, two-way ANOVA, n=3 biological replicates).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of GFAP bands in panel C by densitometry (mean ± SD from three biological replicates; **p<0.01; ****p<0.0001 two-way ANOVA).

strengths: Use of a specific caspase-6 inhibitor (Ac-VEID-CHO) provides pharmacological evidence for caspase-6 involvement.
Testing both S13D alone and S13D/R79H double mutant demonstrates the effect in the context of an AxD mutation.
Strong statistical significance for the double mutant (p<0.0001) with n=3 biological replicates.
The experiment directly addresses the mechanism of cleavage.
weaknesses: Ac-VEID-CHO is not entirely specific for caspase-6; it can inhibit other caspases at higher concentrations.
Only one concentration of inhibitor appears to have been tested (10 µM for 48 hr).
n=3 biological replicates is adequate but not large.
alternative_interpretations: The inhibitor could be affecting other caspases or cellular processes that indirectly reduce GFAP cleavage.
The reduction in cleavage could be due to reduced cellular stress from caspase inhibition rather than direct blockade of GFAP cleavage.
required_assumptions: Ac-VEID-CHO is sufficiently specific for caspase-6 at the concentration used.
The reduction in cleaved GFAP reflects direct caspase-6-mediated cleavage rather than an indirect effect.
evaluation.notes: This is one of the stronger mechanistic experiments in the paper.

nodes.label: Caspase-6 inhibitor Ac-VEID-CHO reduced both the size of S13D aggregates and the…
nodes.claim: Caspase-6 inhibitor Ac-VEID-CHO reduced both the size of S13D aggregates and the presence of ~100 kDa hmm GFAP oligomers (p<0.01, unpaired t-test, n=3).
nodes.verbatim_quote: we found that it reduced both the size of the S13D aggregates and the presence of ~100 kDa hmm GFAP oligomers...n = 3; **p<0.01; unpaired t-test.

strengths: Two independent readouts (aggregate size by IF and hmm oligomers by WB) both show reduction with inhibitor.
Statistical significance for hmm reduction (p<0.01, n=3).
Links caspase-6 activity to both cleavage and aggregation/oligomerization.
weaknesses: Aggregate size reduction is based on representative images without quantitative morphometric analysis.
Despite reducing oligomers, the inhibitor did not fully resolve aggregates — filament bundles were still observed.
The authors acknowledge that caspase-6 appears to regulate both aggregation and normal filament re-organization, complicating therapeutic implications.
Ac-VEID-CHO specificity concerns apply here as well.
alternative_interpretations: Reduction in aggregate size could reflect reduced cellular toxicity from caspase inhibition rather than a direct effect on GFAP aggregation.
The filament bundling seen with inhibitor treatment suggests caspase-6 has a complex role in GFAP dynamics beyond simple cleavage.
required_assumptions: hmm GFAP oligomers are meaningful intermediates in the aggregation pathway.
Aggregate size reduction is a valid proxy for improved GFAP proteostasis.
evaluation.notes: The inability to fully resolve aggregation even with caspase inhibition is an important finding that limits the therapeutic implications.

nodes.label: D225E reduced S13D GFAP cleavage by >90% (p<0.0001 compared to S13D, one-way ANO…
nodes.claim: D225E reduced S13D GFAP cleavage by >90% (p<0.0001 compared to S13D, one-way ANOVA, n=3 biological replicates).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of the abundance of cleaved GFAP in the three mutants shown in panel A relative to WT GFAP (mean ± SD from three biological replicates; ****p<0.0001 compared to S13D; one-way ANOVA).

strengths: >90% reduction in cleavage is a strong effect.
Mutagenesis of the cleavage site provides genetic evidence complementary to pharmacological inhibition.
Strong statistical significance (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA, n=3).
Confirms the specific cleavage site at D225.
weaknesses: D225E mutation itself caused filament bundling and perinuclear structures, complicating interpretation of rescue.
The D225E mutation may alter GFAP structure beyond simply preventing cleavage.
Only partial rescue of filament structure was observed, suggesting cleavage is not the sole mechanism of aggregation.
alternative_interpretations: The partial rescue could indicate that phospho-mimic S13D has aggregation-promoting effects independent of caspase cleavage.
The bundling phenotype of D225E alone suggests this residue may have structural importance beyond being a caspase site.
required_assumptions: D225E specifically prevents caspase-6 cleavage without affecting other GFAP properties.
The 24 kDa fragment detected by GA5 is exclusively generated by cleavage at D225.
evaluation.notes: The fact that D225E alone causes abnormal filament organization is an important caveat that the authors report transparently.

nodes.label: Immunoblot of total brain lysates shows caspase-6 protein in all 8 young AxD pat…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot of total brain lysates shows caspase-6 protein in all 8 young AxD patients and absence in the 5 older AxD patients.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Immunoblot for caspase-6 in total lysates from human AxD post mortem brain tissue shows that caspase-6 is upregulated in young AxD patients.

strengths: Clear binary result: caspase-6 detected in all 8 young patients and essentially absent in 5 older patients.
The finding parallels the pSer13-GFAP results, providing internal consistency across two independent markers.
Uses total brain lysates rather than extracted fractions, reducing potential bias from extraction procedures.
weaknesses: Sample sizes remain small (8 vs 5).
Immunoblot is semi-quantitative; a more quantitative method (e.g., ELISA, qPCR for mRNA) would strengthen the claim.
Post-mortem caspase-6 protein levels could be affected by tissue preservation and post-mortem interval.
The absence/presence dichotomy may not capture more nuanced quantitative differences.
alternative_interpretations: Caspase-6 could be upregulated as a general response to severe neurodegeneration rather than being specific to AxD pathogenesis.
Young patients die from more severe disease, and caspase-6 upregulation could be a consequence rather than a contributor to severity.
required_assumptions: Caspase-6 protein levels in post-mortem tissue reflect in vivo expression levels.
Pan-actin is an adequate normalization control across samples of different ages and disease severity.
evaluation.notes: The authors appropriately do not claim causality — they describe caspase-6 as a 'marker' of severe AxD.

nodes.label: Comparison of caspase-6 levels by densitometry (normalized to actin) in young an…
nodes.claim: Comparison of caspase-6 levels by densitometry (normalized to actin) in young and old AxD vs. age-matched non-AxD controls showed significant increase only in young AxD patients (p<0.01, two-way ANOVA).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of band intensities in panel B by densitometry of caspase-6 normalized to actin. **p<0.01; two-way ANOVA.

strengths: Age-matched non-AxD controls are the appropriate comparison to rule out age as a confounder.
Two-way ANOVA is the correct statistical approach for the 2x2 design (young/old x AxD/control).
p<0.01 provides reasonable statistical confidence.
This experiment directly addresses the potential confound that caspase-6 might simply be higher in young brains.
weaknesses: Sample sizes per group are not clearly stated for this specific comparison, but given the total cohort sizes they are likely very small (n=3-5 per group).
Post-mortem interval and cause of death for controls are potential confounders.
Densitometry of immunoblots provides only semi-quantitative data.
alternative_interpretations: Even among young individuals, the non-AxD controls presumably did not have severe neurodegeneration, so the comparison addresses age but not disease severity in general.
required_assumptions: Non-AxD controls are otherwise neurologically normal.
The comparison is not confounded by systematic differences in tissue quality between AxD and control samples.
evaluation.notes: This is a well-designed control experiment that strengthens the AxD-specificity of the caspase-6 finding.

nodes.label: Western blot of cleaved GFAP (D225 antibody) in AxD brain HSEs showed significan…
nodes.claim: Western blot of cleaved GFAP (D225 antibody) in AxD brain HSEs showed significantly higher D225 signal in young versus old patients (p<0.01, unpaired t-test).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Quantification of band intensities from panel D by densitometry of D225, normalized to total GFAP (**p<0.01, unpaired t-test).

strengths: Uses the specific D225 antibody that recognizes caspase-6-cleaved GFAP, validated by Chen et al. (2013).
Normalization to total GFAP controls for differences in GFAP levels between patients.
Statistical significance achieved (p<0.01, unpaired t-test).
Results parallel the pSer13 and caspase-6 findings, providing convergent evidence.
weaknesses: Small sample sizes (8 young vs 5 old).
HSE preparation could selectively enrich or deplete cleaved fragments depending on their solubility.
The D225 antibody recognizes the N-terminal fragment; it is unclear whether the C-terminal fragment was also examined.
Post-mortem protein degradation could generate non-specific fragments detected by the antibody.
alternative_interpretations: Increased cleaved GFAP could result from greater overall protein turnover in severe disease rather than specific caspase-6 activity.
Post-mortem caspase activation could be more pronounced in brains from young patients who died acutely.
required_assumptions: The D225 antibody specifically detects caspase-6-generated GFAP fragments and not other degradation products.
HSE preparation preserves the relative abundance of cleaved vs. full-length GFAP.
evaluation.notes: The convergence of three independent markers (pSer13, caspase-6 protein, D225 cleavage) in the same patient group is compelling despite individual limitations.

nodes.label: Brain tissue immunofluorescence shows widespread cleaved GFAP (D225) staining in…
nodes.claim: Brain tissue immunofluorescence shows widespread cleaved GFAP (D225) staining in cortex and white matter of a 347-day-old AxD child, but low expression in a 42-year-old AxD patient.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Immunofluorescence staining showing widespread presence of cleaved GFAP (D225; magenta) in cerebral cortex and underlying white matter of 347 day-old child with AxD and low expression of cleaved GFAP in a 42 year old AxD patient.

strengths: Immunofluorescence provides spatial information showing regional distribution of cleaved GFAP in brain tissue.
Perinuclear localization with DAPI-positive structures parallels findings in iPSC-astrocytes, providing cross-system validation.
Additional patients and wider fields of view are referenced in supplementary figures.
weaknesses: Only two representative patients are shown in the main figure (one young, one old).
The comparison is qualitative ('widespread' vs. 'low expression') without quantitative image analysis.
Differences in tissue fixation, processing, or section thickness could affect staining intensity between samples.
The 347-day-old child and 42-year-old patient may differ in many ways beyond age/severity.
alternative_interpretations: Regional differences in GFAP expression could account for some of the staining differences.
Post-mortem autolysis could differentially affect tissue from different patients.
required_assumptions: Tissue processing was comparable between the two patients shown.
D225 antibody staining intensity correlates with the amount of caspase-6-cleaved GFAP.
evaluation.notes: This provides important spatial context but would benefit from more systematic quantification across patients.

nodes.label: Immunoblot quantification showed significantly higher GFAP in AxD patient and CR…
nodes.claim: Immunoblot quantification showed significantly higher GFAP in AxD patient and CRISPR control lines versus isogenic control (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
nodes.verbatim_quote: ****p<0.0001 compared to isogenic control; one-way ANOVA.

strengths: Strong statistical significance (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
Isogenic control provides the ideal comparison, eliminating genetic background as a confounder.
Both AxD patient and CRISPR control (which retains the mutation) show elevated GFAP, confirming mutation-dependence.
Consistent with in vivo observations in AxD patients (Jany et al., 2015) and mouse models (Jany et al., 2013).
Multiple loading controls are used (actin and Coomassie stain).
weaknesses: The number of biological replicates for the immunoblot quantification is not clearly stated.
Only one patient mutation (R239C) is modeled; generalizability to other AxD mutations is assumed but not tested.
iPSC-derived astrocytes may not fully recapitulate mature astrocyte physiology.
alternative_interpretations: Elevated GFAP could partly reflect differences in differentiation efficiency between lines, though the CRISPR control argues against this.
required_assumptions: The isogenic control and CRISPR control clones are otherwise genetically identical.
iPSC-astrocyte differentiation is comparable across cell lines.
evaluation.notes: The CRISPR control (edited on WT allele, retaining mutation) is a clever experimental design element that strengthens the conclusion.

nodes.label: Increased levels of cleaved GFAP (normalized to total GFAP) were observed in AxD…
nodes.claim: Increased levels of cleaved GFAP (normalized to total GFAP) were observed in AxD iPSC-astrocytes compared to isogenic controls by immunoblot.
nodes.verbatim_quote: we observed increased levels of cleaved GFAP (upon normalization for total GFAP) in the AxD iPSC-astrocytes compared to isogenic control astrocytes

strengths: Uses the isogenic control as the ideal comparison.
Loading was adjusted to normalize total GFAP levels, allowing comparison of cleaved fragment abundance.
weaknesses: No statistical analysis is reported for this comparison — the claim is based on visual inspection of immunoblots.
The number of replicates is not stated.
Different amounts of total protein were loaded to normalize GFAP monomer levels, which is methodologically unusual and could introduce artifacts.
Without quantification, the term 'increased levels' is imprecise.
alternative_interpretations: Differences in cleaved GFAP could reflect differences in protein turnover or culture conditions rather than disease-specific caspase activity.
Loading different amounts of protein to normalize one band may distort the apparent abundance of other proteins.
required_assumptions: The cleaved GFAP fragment is stable and detectable by the antibody used.
Normalizing by adjusting total protein loaded is equivalent to normalizing by GFAP levels.
The cleaved fragment reflects caspase-6 activity specifically.
evaluation.notes: This claim would be significantly strengthened by quantification with biological replicates and statistical testing. The unusual loading strategy could be questioned by reviewers.

summary.overall_assessment: The paper's 51 claims show mixed overall support when weighted by centrality (weighted support score 0.65, where the central thesis counts far more than peripheral evidence). The most load-bearing weakly-supported claim is: “Whether these PTMs contribute to disease severity or are a consequence of it remains undetermined and requires future interventional studies.” (4 weakly-supported claim(s) total).
